statement: The shipped product-analysis rubric reaches 4 of the 10 defect classes on the audited feature across three independent blind raters, with a per-rater median of 3.
falsification: A re-score of the three E2 artifacts against the frozen corpus finding five or more classes would falsify it.

statement: None of the three baseline artifacts proposes an infrastructure change for a defect whose fix needs an absent layer; all three end in UI and copy recommendations.
falsification: A capability-change proposal located in any of the three artifacts would falsify it.

statement: A browser request log cannot settle a capability row: the audited admin calls the API from the server, so its /users page yields exactly one browser-log entry.
falsification: A run that shows the API call in the page's own request log would falsify it.

statement: Diffing the API's committed contract against the surface's call sites reproduces the two declared-and-unreached users endpoints in 3.09 s with no credential and no running app.
falsification: Re-running the pipeline and getting an empty set difference would falsify it.

statement: Nine of the thirteen frozen corpus rows are invisible from the screen alone: they need a second layer read before the deviation exists.
falsification: A row-by-row review showing a screen-level read reaches more than four of them would falsify the count.

statement: The feature-audit skill ships and its task class is reachable: the committed skill file is registered by the installer, and the product-arming matcher the skill rides on arms on the 8 feature-surface prompts its test carries and stays silent on the 7 negatives beside them (tests/test_context.py, ProductClassArming). The session's own larger sample - 9 positives armed, 0 false arms on 10 negatives - is recorded in log.md and has no run artifact, so it is not part of what this claim asserts.
falsification: A rerun of tests/test_context.py in which the product class fails to arm on one of the eight prompts, or arms on one of the seven negatives, would falsify it.

statement: Every audit tool surveyed at source automates one layer boundary (spec-to-spec, spec-to-store, or surface-to-rule) and none carries a feature's whole path.
falsification: A tool that compares the surface against the store and the route against the policy in one run would falsify it.

statement: With three blind raters per arm on the first feature, the artifact arm reaches 7 defect classes against the pre-wiring rubric's 6 (per-artifact tier-A rows 8/7/6 against 4/6/4), and on the second stack the same comparison reads 6 against 4; but the post-wiring product-analysis skill alone reaches 6 on the second stack, above the artifact's 5, so the wiring is the larger lever and a single reading can move up to three classes.
falsification: A fourth rater per arm on either stack inverting the ordering, or a re-score of the same six artifacts finding arm B at or above arm A's class count, would falsify it.

statement: The capability-change proposal is a property the artifact requires and a rubric without the slot does not: 14 of 14 artifacts that followed feature-audit wrote at least one (22 counted in the eleven read line by line, plus at least one each in E3's raters A-C), against 2 of 5 that followed the pre-wiring rubric under a heading-only reading and 3 of 5 under a content reading - E8-B1 proposing the same absent layers under a recommendations heading and saying so.
falsification: A read of any archived artifact-following artifact finding no capability-change proposal in it, or a recount finding none in three or more of the five control artifacts, would falsify it.

statement: The runtime half carries defect classes a source-only audit cannot state: on the second stack the users table clips its columns at 320 and, with a long row, at 768, with overflow-x hidden and no auto rule anywhere, so the clipped columns are unreachable rather than scrollable - and the repository's own make admin-dev never reaches that surface, its frontend crash-looping on an nginx upstream the dev composition does not start.
falsification: A run in which the surface scrolls to the clipped column, or in which make admin-dev alone reaches it, would falsify it.

statement: Two evidence classes every earlier arm declared unreachable were looked for wrongly, not unreachable: both products carry a wired analytics seam that is disabled at construction (noop sink, switch default off, consent false, and in the first product no caller ever passes enabled), and both carry real user-voice sources (support tickets and messages, a customer-portal free-text request).
falsification: A read showing the analytics client enabled by default, or showing no ticket/message corpus for either product, would falsify it.

statement: The competition axis is producible: seven comparable products read at first hand (URL and date each) all deliver an invitation credential in-product, which makes the audited feature's invitation with no delivery path a market gap and not only an internal inconsistency.
falsification: A reread of the seven sources finding an invitation flow whose credential is only ever delivered out of band would falsify it.

statement: Four of the six first-feature artifacts, and the session's own judgement model, reported a defect at the corpus's pass row where the surface's control and the server's refusal agree - so a corpus that carries only defects cannot show whether an analysis can tell agreement from drift.
falsification: A re-read of the six artifacts finding fewer than three pass-row claims would falsify it.
